newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt up in U.S. but activity remains thin.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt up in U.S. but activity remains thin.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices rose on Friday in line with U.S. Treasury securities but market players said trading activity remained thin ahead of the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.

"The market is up about 1/4 to 1/2 point following the long (U.S. Treasury) bond," said one emerging market debt trader. "We think the market will not trade much during the rest of the afternoon. It is likely to remain range-bound."
One emerging markets debt source noted that the launching of a $750 million global bond issue added to the runup in Brazilian debt assets.
Indeed, Brazilian C bonds BR8D14=RR rose 3/8 to 72-1/4 bid and the country's pars BR4D24=RR firmed 1/4 to 61 bid.

Joint lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg said Friday in London that the roadshows for the deal will be held during the week starting October 21 and presentations will be made in Asia, Europe and the United States.
"There has been a little bit of buying pressure in Brazilian assets on the back of the announcement of the $750 million global bond to be issued by Brazil," one source said.
Also in the pipeline is Russia's Eurobond issue. Market talk in London is 350 basis points.

One market expert noted that excess liquidity in the emerging debt markets continued to drive supply. "A lot of what is creating the runup is liquidity," he said, adding "there is money out there chasing yield."
Meanwhile, South Africa issued a $300 million 10-year yankee bond via Merrill Lynch. The bonds were given an 8-3/8 percent coupon to yield 195 basis points over Treasuries.
One European banker said the issue, South Africa's first Yankee bond, looked like it was priced to sell, with spread talk on the issue lower than the eventual launch spread.
With the issue coming in fairly tight, South Africa could see the deal as a triumph, one U.S. debt analyst said.
South Africa issued a 10-year sterling bond earlier in the year which came at 190 b.p. over, and market talk detailed the government as keen to achieve a spread close to that level.
In the broader market, Mexico's global bond due 2026 MXUMS=RR rose 3/8 to 101-1/8 and Russian Vnesh dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR firmed 3/4 to 79.
